question: Which microphone should live captions use on iPhone?
slides: Captions only work with *the sound they hear.*
iPhone: with AirPods, Captio AI asks *which microphone.*
description: For live captions on iPhone, connect the microphone you want and pick it when Captio AI asks which one captions should use.
Captio AI is made for deaf and hard of hearing people who follow talk in the same room, so the microphone choice sits inside the app.
A 2021 Frontiers in Neuroscience study of 23 adults with hearing loss in China found a remote microphone improved signal-to-noise ratio by 11 to 19.5 dB over directional hearing aids.
The same 2021 study compared hearing aid microphones with a wireless microphone, not phones or AirPods, so it shows only that sound picked up near the talker is clearer.
Apple Support says AirPods use either AirPod as the microphone by default, and you can fix it to the left or right AirPod in Settings.
Captio AI, on iPhone, asks which connected microphone captions should use when AirPods or another microphone is connected, and remembers your choice, according to its version 1.1.6 release notes.
For live captions at a lecture or a meeting, sitting nearer the speaker, or putting your phone close to the people talking, is our suggestion, not a tested result.
Captio AI is free to download on the App Store, and the free plan includes 100 free credits a day, as of October 2026.
Captions need an internet connection and may contain mistakes, so check medical instructions with your doctor or pharmacist, and Captio AI is no substitute for an interpreter.
